([[Shoreline, Washington]]) | college = [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] (2017–2021) | highlights = * Consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2021 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2021]]) * [[Julius Erving Award]] (2021) * [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|WCC Player of the Year]] ([[2020–21 West Coast Conference men's basketball season|2021]]) * 2× First-team All-[[West Coast Conference|WCC]] ([[2019–20 West Coast Conference men's basketball season|2020]], [[2020–21 West Coast Conference men's basketball season|2021]]) * [[List of Men's Basketball Academic All-America Team Members of the Year|Academic All-American of the Year]] (2021) }} '''Corey James Kispert''' (born March 3, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga Bulldogs]]. ==High school career== Kispert grew up in [[Edmonds, Washington]] and attended [[King's High School]]. As a junior, he averaged 23.9 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.3 steals per game, led the team to their second straight state title, and was named the MVP of the State Championship Tournament.{{cite web|url=https://www.spokesman.com/blogs/sportslink/2016/may/04/kispert-commits-gonzaga/|title=Kispert commits to Gonzaga|first=Jim|last=Meehan|work=The Spokesman-Review|date=May 4, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}} Rated a four-star recruit, Kispert committed to play college basketball at [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] after his junior season.{{cite web|url=https://notredame.rivals.com/news/corey-kispert-sets-notre-dame-visit|title=Corey Kispert Sets Notre Dame Visit|first=Jordan|last=Wells|website=Rivals.com|date=April 7, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2638011-corey-kispert-to-gonzaga-bulldogs-land-4-star-sf-prospect|title=Corey Kispert to Gonzaga: Bulldogs Land 4-Star SF Prospect|first=Scott|last=Polacek|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=May 4, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2019}} Kispert was averaging 25 points per game during his senior year before breaking his foot in February.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/high-school/kings-corey-kispert-a-gonzaga-signee-out-for-season-with-broken-bone-in-foot/|title=King’s Corey Kispert, a Gonzaga signee, out for season with broken bone in foot|first=Sandy|last=Ringer|work=The Seattle Times|date=February 19, 2017|access-date=December 26, 2019}} Kispert said in 2021 that [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] head coach [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] told Kispert he "needed to see Corey play more against top competition before deciding if he could play at Virginia" and that motivated him to "stick it to" Virginia in an early season game; Virginia had recruited Kispert but did not offer him a scholarship before he committed to Gonzaga."[https://www.essentiallysports.com/ncaa-college-basketball-news-gonzaga-bulldogs-corey-kispert-reveals-how-virginia-cavaliers-tony-bennett-motivated-him-to-kick-their-a/ Corey Kispert Claims Tony Bennett Told Him He Wasn't Good Enough To Play, So Kispert Dropped 32 Against Virginia To 'Stick It To Him']". Essentially Sports, April 22, 2021. Accessed April 22, 2021. ==College career== As a true freshman Kispert played in all 35 of Gonzaga's games with seven starts, averaging 6.7 points and 3.2 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.slipperstillfits.com/2019/10/8/20904190/2019-20-player-preview-corey-kispert|title=2019-20 Player Preview: Corey Kispert|website=SlipperStillFits.com|first=Megan|last=Stoudt|date=October 8, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}} He became a starter for the Bulldogs going into his sophomore season, averaging 8.0 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/gonzaga-bulldogs/edmonds-native-corey-kispert-has-been-a-difference-maker-for-gonzaa-oh-yeah-and-hes-got-great-hair/|title=Edmonds native Corey Kispert has been a difference maker for Gonzaga. Oh yeah, and he’s got great hair.|first=Matt|last=Calkins|work=The Seattle Times|date=March 28, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://theathletic.com/1294674/2019/10/22/is-gonzagas-corey-kispert-ready-for-a-larger-offensive-role/|title=Is Gonzaga’s Corey Kispert ready for a larger offensive role?|first=Jackson|last=Frank|website=[[The Athletic]]|date=October 22, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}} Kispert entered his junior season on the [[Julius Erving Award]] watchlist and as Gonzaga's only returning starter from the previous year.{{cite web|url=https://www.heraldnet.com/sports/local-players-named-to-preseason-college-hoops-watch-lists/|title=Local players named to preseason college hoops watch lists|first=Nick|last=Patterson|work=[[The Herald (Everett)|The Herald]]|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401175199|title=Kispert leads No. 8 Gonzaga over Alabama State 95-64|website=ESPN.com|publisher=Associated Press|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}} After scoring less than five points in his previous three games, Kispert scored 28 points and made seven of eight three point attempts on November 28, 2019 against [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles basketball|Southern Mississippi]] in the opening round of the [[Battle 4 Atlantis#2019|2019 Battle 4 Atlantis]].{{cite web|url=https://apnews.com/de4fc396adb849fca09afafd330dc835|title=Kispert, No. 8 Gonzaga top Southern Miss 94–69 at Atlantis|first=Aaron|last=Beard|website=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 28, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}} He scored 26 points with five three pointers made against [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in a 94–81 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401168261|title=No. 2 Gonzaga leaves North Carolina blue after 94–81 victory|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=December 18, 2019|access-date=December 26, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Kispert was named to the First Team All-[[West Coast Conference]].{{cite press release|url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/3/3/wcc-announces-2019-20-mens-basketball-all-conference-team-mbb.aspx |title=WCC Announces 2019-20 Men's Basketball All-Conference Team |publisher=West Coast Conference |date=March 3, 2020 |accessdate=March 3, 2020}} Kispert averaged 13.9 points per game as a junior.{{cite news |title=No. 2 Gonzaga looks to extend streak vs No. 23 BYU |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/no-gonzaga-looks-to-extend-streak-vs-no-byu/article_5b3438a0-90b9-5814-95ca-3bc5d8f2beb0.html |accessdate=March 16, 2020 |work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 21, 2020}} Following the season, he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]] but did not hire an agent.{{cite news |last1=Helin |first1=Kurt |title=Gonzaga’s Corey Kispert declares for NBA draft, does not hire agent |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/04/25/gonzagas-corey-kispert-declares-for-nba-draft/ |accessdate=May 1, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=April 25, 2020}} Kispert ultimately decided to return for his senior season on August 3.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Gonzaga boosted by Corey Kispert's decision to return |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29589519/gonzaga-boosted-corey-kispert-decision-return |accessdate=August 4, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=August 3, 2020}} Coming into his senior season, Kispert was named to the Preseason All-[[West Coast Conference]] team.{{cite web |title=Gonzaga Picked to Win Ninth Straight WCC Championship |url=https://wccsports.com/news/2020/10/25/mens-basketball-gonzaga-picked-to-win-ninth-straight-wcc-championship.aspx |website=[[West Coast Conference]] |accessdate=November 7, 2020 |date=October 26, 2020}} He scored his 1,000th career point in the season opener against [[2020–21 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]] as part of a 23-point performance in the 102–90 victory.{{cite web|url=https://www.khq.com/sports/gonzaga/updates-no-1-gonzaga-opens-season-against-no-6-kansas/article_e9eb0b0a-ee15-5fcf-8745-3e95f051c25c.html|title=Recap and highlights: No. 1 Gonzaga beats No. 6 Kansas in season opener|website=[[KHQ-TV|KHQ.com]]|date=November 26, 2020|access-date=November 27, 2020}} On December 26, 2020, Kispert scored a career-high 32 points, tying the school record with nine three-pointers, in a 98–75 win against [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].{{cite web |title=Kispert’s career game leads No. 1 Gonzaga over No. 16 Virginia |url=https://www.heraldnet.com/sports/kisperts-career-game-leads-no-1-gonzaga-over-no-16-virginia/ |website=[[The Everett Herald]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=December 26, 2020}} He led Gonzaga to a 31–1 record, its only loss coming against [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] in the [[2021 NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Tournament|national championship game]].{{cite web |title=Nobody’s perfect: Gonzaga men lose to Baylor in national-title game, end season 31-1 |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/gonzaga-bulldogs/nobodys-perfect-gonzaga-men-lose-to-baylor-in-national-title-game-end-season-31-1/ |website=[[The Seattle Times]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=April 5, 2021}} Kispert was named [[West Coast Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|WCC Player of the Year]] and won the Julius Erving Award as the top [[small forward]] in the nation.{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Gonzaga's Corey Kispert named Julius Erving Award winner as nation's top small forward |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/apr/03/gonzagas-corey-kispert-named-julius-erving-award-w/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=April 3, 2021}} As a senior, he averaged 18.6 points and five rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Meehan |first1=Jim |title=Corey Kispert named WCC player of year, Gonzaga dominates conference awards |url=https://www.spokesman.com/stories/2021/mar/02/corey-kispert-named-player-of-year-gonzaga-dominat/ |website=[[The Spokesman-Review]] |access-date=July 21, 2021 |date=March 2, 2021}} ==Career
